description: Watch every git repository under one folder in a live table.

options.description: Folder holding the repositories to watch, as an absolute path. Without it repo-master asks for one the first time it is run and writes the answer here; with nobody to ask — a pipe, --once — it watches the directory it is run in.
How many folders deep to look for repositories.
Seconds between full sweeps: a rescan for repositories that came or went, plus a git refresh of every row.

The folders to leave out of the table, written in git's own syntax and read in the watched folder — one folder to a line, # for a comment, ! to let one back in. The default looks for .giftignore first and falls back to .gitignore. A name is read as a path when it holds a slash, and an absolute path is read where it is. Empty leaves nothing out.
Command behind `goto folder` — the shell started in the chosen repository. Without it, your login shell from $SHELL.
Command behind `open with code` and the `e` key — `cursor` and `windsurf` take a folder the same way.
Command behind `open with vim` and the `v` key — `nvim`, `hx` and the like take a file the same way.

The picker `open with vim` asks which file with, before vim opens it. It is given the terminal and read for what it prints, so anything that lists a choice and prints it will do. Without it installed, vim opens the folder instead. It lists the files with `fd`, which leaves out whatever .gitignore does, and previews them with `bat` — falling back to git's own file list and to `cat` where those are missing, and to your $FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND for the list where you have set one.
The option `open with claude code` passes the repositories picked after the main one, once per repository. Set it to false to open the main project alone.
The same for `open with codex`, for a version that spells the option differently.
